Somerville.narrative: Somerville's real estate market remains exceptionally tight across all property types, with virtually no measurable months of supply and brisk sales volume — 53 total transactions closed in the past 30 days spanning singles, condos, and multi-families. Single-family homes commanded a median of $1,055,000 with 40% of sales closing above list price, while condos moved at a healthy $849,950 median and a near-perfect 99.8% sale-to-list ratio, signaling that even the city's most active segment leaves little room for negotiation. Multi-family properties led the pack on price at a $1,354,500 median, though the 16.7% over-ask rate and 97.6% SP/LP ratio suggest investors are being slightly more disciplined — yet still competitive. For buyers, this market demands pre-approval, speed, and strong offers from day one; for sellers, the data confirms that well-priced Somerville properties are effectively selling themselves, often above asking and within days of hitting the market.

Cambridge.narrative: Cambridge remains one of the most competitive markets in Greater Boston, with single-family homes commanding a median sale price of $2,337,500 and condos moving at a median of $866,610 — both segments closing essentially at or above list price, with 41-42% of properties selling over asking. Multi-families are fetching a median of $2,402,500, though buyers in that segment are securing slightly more negotiating room with a 95.3% SP/LP ratio and one-third still closing above list. With effectively zero months of supply across all property types and 44 condos and 12 single-families transacting in just the last 30 days, inventory is being absorbed almost instantly. Sellers are in an exceptionally strong position to price confidently and expect swift, competitive offers, while buyers should come prepared with pre-approval in hand, minimal contingencies, and the financial flexibility to escalate well above list price to have a realistic shot at securing a property.

Milton.narrative: Milton's real estate market is exceptionally competitive across all property types, with single-family homes commanding a median sale price of $1,130,000 and selling right at list price on average, while a striking 42.1% of those 19 homes sold in the past 30 days closed above asking. The condo market is similarly tight at a $725,000 median, and multi-family properties are the hottest segment of all — with half of the 2 sales closing over ask and a median price of $1,238,000, buyers are clearly willing to pay a premium for income-producing assets in this sought-after town. With effectively zero months of supply across every category, Milton is operating in a deeply undersupplied market where sellers hold enormous leverage and well-priced listings are generating immediate, competitive offers. Buyers should come prepared with strong pre-approvals, flexible terms, and realistic expectations about bidding above list price, as hesitation in this market typically means losing out entirely.

Quincy.narrative: Quincy's real estate market remains fiercely competitive across all property types, with single families commanding a median of $770,000 and nearly half of all homes — 46.2% — selling above asking price at exactly list price on average, signaling that well-priced properties are attracting multiple offers and bidding wars. Condos offer a more accessible entry point at a $440,000 median, though 31% still close over ask, while multi-families are fetching a hefty $1,056,000 median with 14.3% selling above list. With inventory so tight that months of supply is effectively zero across all segments and 62 total transactions closed in the past 30 days, sellers are in an exceptionally strong position to achieve full price or better with minimal time on market. Buyers should come prepared with pre-approvals in hand, flexible terms, and the willingness to move quickly and competitively — especially in the single-family segment where over-ask offers have become the norm rather than the exception.

Watertown.narrative: Watertown's real estate market remains fiercely competitive across all property types, with single-family homes leading the charge at a median sale price of $1,110,000 and an eye-popping 105.1% sale-to-list ratio — meaning every single home sold in the past 30 days went above asking price. Condos offer a relatively more accessible entry point at a $575,000 median, though 38.1% still sold over list at a 99.0% SP/LP ratio, and multi-families commanded a $1,100,000 median with 42.9% selling above ask. With essentially no months of supply recorded across all three categories and only 3 single-family homes trading hands in the last 30 days, inventory is critically tight, giving sellers extraordinary leverage and the realistic expectation of multiple offers and above-list results. Buyers should come prepared with strong pre-approvals, escalation clauses, and minimal contingencies — particularly for single-family properties, where the competition is most intense and the price of hesitation is steep.

Medford.narrative: Medford's real estate market is firing on all cylinders, with single-family homes commanding a median sale price of $975,000 and a staggering 58.1% of properties selling above asking price at an average of 100.1% of list price — a clear signal that buyer competition remains fierce. Multi-family properties are the hottest asset class in town, with a median sale price of $1,171,000 and 75% of homes selling over ask at 102.4% of list, reflecting strong investor and owner-occupant demand for income-producing properties. Condos offer a comparatively accessible entry point at a $644,500 median, though even that segment is seeing full list-price sales with more than one in four units going above asking. With essentially no months of supply across all property types and 53 total sales in the past 30 days, sellers hold nearly all the leverage, while buyers should come prepared with aggressive offers, minimal contingencies, and pre-approval letters in hand.

Melrose.narrative: Melrose remains one of the North Shore's most competitive markets, with single-family homes selling at a median of $922,000 and flying off the market at 110.5% of list price — a staggering 82.4% of those homes closing above asking. Multi-families are even more aggressive, with all three sales in the past 30 days closing above ask at a median of $1,099,000 and a 110% sale-to-list ratio, signaling strong investor and owner-occupant demand for income-producing properties. Condos offer a comparatively calmer entry point at a $475,000 median with a near-par 99.4% sale-to-list ratio, though even that segment saw over a quarter of units sell above asking. With virtually no months of supply across all property types, sellers hold extraordinary leverage right now, while buyers should expect to move fast, waive contingencies strategically, and come prepared to bid well over list — especially on single-family and multi-family properties.

Arlington.narrative: Arlington's real estate market remains fiercely competitive across all property types, with single-family homes posting a median sale price of $1,377,500 and condos closing at $850,000, while multi-families command a median of $1,327,500 — all selling at or essentially at full list price. With half of all multi-family sales and 45% of single-family sales closing above asking price, and inventory so tight that months of supply is effectively zero, demand is dramatically outpacing what's available. For sellers, conditions couldn't be much stronger — properly priced homes are generating multiple offers and near-instant sales, with 20 single-family and 13 condo transactions completed in just the past 30 days despite the slim pickings. Buyers should expect to move quickly, come in at or above list price, and have financing thoroughly buttoned up before stepping foot through a door in this market.

Belmont.narrative: Belmont's real estate market remains fiercely competitive across all property types, with single-family homes commanding a median sale price of $1,494,500 and 70% of properties selling above asking — the average sale coming in at 100.5% of list price. Condos are equally aggressive at a $1,015,000 median with 102.6% SP/LP ratio, while the lone multi-family sale in the past 30 days closed at a striking 105.8% of list price with all transactions going over ask. With effectively zero months of supply across every category, this is an inventory-starved market where sellers hold enormous leverage and can confidently expect multiple offers and above-list outcomes. Buyers should be prepared to move quickly, waive contingencies strategically, and come to the table with strong pre-approvals — hesitation in Belmont right now is almost certainly a losing strategy.

Winchester.narrative: Winchester's single-family market is firing on all cylinders, with a median sale price of $1.7 million and 57.9% of homes selling above asking price at an average of 100.7% of list price — a clear signal that well-priced inventory is generating immediate, competitive interest. Condos are equally tight, with a $964,500 median and half of all units selling over ask, while multi-families are the lone segment showing any negotiating room, closing at 97.7% of list with no homes going above asking. With essentially no months of supply across all property types and 19 single-family homes trading hands in just the last 30 days, inventory is being absorbed as fast as it hits the market. Sellers in Winchester hold significant leverage right now and should expect strong offers quickly, while buyers need to come prepared with sharp pricing strategies, minimal contingencies, and the financial flexibility to move fast — particularly in the single-family and condo segments where bidding wars remain the norm.

Boston.narrative: Boston's real estate market remains intensely competitive across all property types, with single-family homes commanding a median sale price of $950,000 and selling at exactly list price on average, while a striking 45.6% of those homes closed above asking — a clear signal that well-priced inventory is triggering bidding wars. Condos are the most active segment with 289 sales in the past 30 days at a median of $750,000 and 98.7% of list price, while multi-families are fetching a median of $1,200,000 with nearly 30% selling over ask, reflecting strong investor and owner-occupant demand for income-producing properties. With months of supply data effectively at zero across all categories, Boston is operating in a severe supply crunch that gives sellers exceptional leverage — properly priced homes are moving fast and often sparking multiple-offer scenarios. For buyers, this market demands preparation: pre-approval in hand, an experienced agent, and the readiness to move decisively and potentially waive contingencies to remain competitive.
